run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Social Network
Namespace: social-network

A social network with unidirectional follow relationships, implemented with loosely-coupled microservices, communicating with each other via Thrift RPCs.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The social-network frontend is down because its pod runs under a 16Mi memory limit injected at pod admission. ConfigMap platform-ops/platform-policy-controller-server holds server.py with MEMORY = "16Mi", which emits JSONPatch ops that stamp requests.memory and limits.memory = 16Mi onto /spec/containers/0 of every admitted pod; the Deployment platform-ops/platform-policy-controller (python /app/server.py, created 09:34:35) serves that code behind five MutatingWebhookConfigurations, all scoped to namespace social-network with failurePolicy Fail. The only social-network pod created after the controller became ready, nginx-thrift-65f656c999-ws8sl (created 09:34:46), is also the only pod in the cluster carrying a 16Mi memory limit - its owning ReplicaSet and Deployment templates still declare 256Mi/128Mi, and its managedFields show only kube-controller-manager creation, i.e. the resources were set in the admitting CREATE, not by a later patch. That container was OOMKilled (exit 137) 10 s after start, and by 09:36-09:37 it was in CrashLoopBackOff with 3-4 restarts. Consequence observed on the frontend itself: Service nginx-thrift (ClusterIP 10.96.157.218:8080 - the load generator's target) has zero ready endpoints and lists the pod only in notReadyAddresses, and the wrk2 load generator's throughput collapsed from 102.08 req/s (round #0, 8 write socket errors) to 28.98 req/s (round #1, 7318 write socket errors, 9 timeouts). Backend services looked healthy in the sampled traces just before the crash loop (HTTP 200 nginx-web-server spans and zero error rows across compose-post, text, user-timeline, home-timeline, social-graph, post-storage, url-shorten, user-mention, unique-id, media and user services, ms-scale durations), and the nodes had 64-68% memory available, so neither node pressure nor the 256Mi deployment-level limit explains the kill (the same-template pod gvltj peaked at ~4.2 MB). The link from the ConfigMap code to this specific pod is an inference from the code, the timing and the unique 16Mi value: the admission review itself was not captured (the webhook writes no logs) and is recorded as a gap.

claims.text: Pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-ws8sl (namespace social-network) runs container nginx-thrift with resources limits.memory=16Mi and requests.memory=16Mi.
Its owner ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-65f656c999 and Deployment nginx-thrift declare limits.memory=256Mi and requests.memory=128Mi, so the running pod deviates from its own workload template.
Across all pods in the cluster, nginx-thrift-65f656c999-ws8sl is the only pod whose first container carries a 16Mi memory limit; all other social-network pods have no memory limits at all.

ConfigMap platform-ops/platform-policy-controller-server contains server.py with MEMORY = "16Mi" and build_patch() emitting JSONPatch add ops for /spec/containers/0/resources/requests/memory and /spec/containers/0/resources/limits/memory on each admitted pod.

Deployment platform-ops/platform-policy-controller (1 replica, command python /app/server.py, created 2026-11-24T09:34:35Z by kubectl-client-side-apply) has its pod platform-policy-controller-7d44bbdc6b-pfqf2 Running, ready and with 0 restarts.

Five MutatingWebhookConfigurations that match pods (cert-manager-webhook, gatekeeper-mutating-webhook-configuration, istio-sidecar-injector, kyverno-resource-mutating-webhook-cfg, linkerd-proxy-injector-webhook-config) all resolve to service platform-ops/platform-policy-controller with namespaceSelector kubernetes.io/metadata.name=social-network and failurePolicy Fail; gatekeeper-mutating-webhook-configuration matches all pods on CREATE with no objectSelector.

Timing matches admission-time injection: every other social-network pod was created 09:34:25-09:34:29 (before the policy controller pod existed at 09:34:35) and has no limits, while nginx-thrift-65f656c999-ws8sl was created 09:34:46 (after it).

The 16Mi resources were not written by a later patch: the pod's managedFieldsSummary lists only kube-controller-manager Update at 09:34:46 plus status writers, and ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-65f656c999 lists only kube-controller-manager writes and still holds the 256Mi template.

Container nginx-thrift in pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-ws8sl terminated with exit code 137: at 09:35:09 its lastState was terminated reason OOMKilled (startedAt 09:34:47Z, finishedAt 09:34:57Z), by 09:36:43 it had 3 restarts and state waiting reason CrashLoopBackOff (back-off 40s), and by 09:37:40 it had 4 restarts.

Service nginx-thrift (ClusterIP 10.96.157.218, port 8080, selector service=nginx-thrift) has no ready endpoint addresses; pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-ws8sl (10.244.7.201) appears only under notReadyAddresses, so the social-network HTTP frontend has no ready backend.

The wrk2 load generator hitting http://10.96.157.218:8080/wrk2-api/post/compose reported 102.08 req/s with 8 write socket errors for round #0, then 290 requests in 10.01 s (28.98 req/s) with 7318 write socket errors and 9 timeouts for round #1 (started 09:34:43Z, result 09:34:53Z).

Sampled Jaeger traces for nginx-web-server between 09:34:38 and 09:34:46 show /wrk2-api/post/compose, /wrk2-api/home-timeline/read and /wrk2-api/user-timeline/read with http.status_code=200, and the downstream spans (compose-post-service, text-service, user-timeline-service, home-timeline-service, social-graph-service, post-storage-service, url-shorten-service, user-mention-service, unique-id-service, media-service, user-service) have error_rows 0 with ms-scale durations.

Deployment nginx-thrift was updated at 09:34:32 by manager kubectl-patch (generation 2), which created ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-65f656c999 with the same image digest and rolled the pod to nginx-thrift-65f656c999-gvltj.
All four nodes had 64-68% of memory available at 09:34:57, so the exit-137 kill was not a node-level memory-pressure eviction.

The 256Mi limit declared by the nginx-thrift Deployment/ReplicaSet did not cause the kill: the pod created from that template, nginx-thrift-65f656c999-gvltj, reported container_spec_memory_limit_bytes=268435456 with container_memory_max_usage_bytes about 4.2MB and working set about 2.35MB.

nginx-thrift container logs show 'worker process <n> exited on signal 11' at 09:34:34Z for pod nginx-thrift-68bc7d94df-477lv and at 09:34:46Z for pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-gvltj, both at the moments those pods were being stopped/deleted (Pod Killing events at 09:34:34Z and 09:34:46Z).

The observed nginx worker SIGSEGV (signal 11) lines are a shutdown artefact of the two pods being deleted during the 09:34:32-09:34:46 rollouts rather than the cause of the current failure; the crash-looping pod's failure is an exit-137 kill under a 16Mi cgroup limit and no signal-11 line was captured for it.

While the mutating webhook stays active (Deployment platform-policy-controller running, failurePolicy Fail, namespaceSelector social-network), any further pod created in social-network will also receive the 16Mi memory request/limit on container[0] and risk the same OOM loop; only nginx-thrift-65f656c999-ws8sl has been observed affected so far.

Correct or remove the 16Mi memory injection (ConfigMap platform-policy-controller-server in platform-ops and/or the pod-mutating webhook configurations pointing at platform-policy-controller) and delete pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-ws8sl so the Deployment recreates it with the intended 256Mi/128Mi; then verify the new pod's limits and that the nginx-thrift Endpoints gain a ready address.

gaps: The admission review that stamped 16Mi onto pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-ws8sl was not directly observed: the policy controller's container writes no log output (log_message is disabled in server.py and its pod log is empty), so the link from the ConfigMap code to this specific pod is an inference from the code, the timing (pod created 12 s after the controller pod) and the unique 16Mi value.

No application RED metrics were available: trace/RPC metrics such as traces_span_metrics_calls_total, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count and http_server_request_duration_seconds_count returned no series from the queried Prometheus (which exposes mainly cadvisor/node/kube-state metrics), so service error rates and latency baselines could not be measured and health of backend services rests on the Jaeger sample only.

The crash-looping container's own output was not readable: fetch_pod_logs returned no lines for nginx-thrift-65f656c999-ws8sl (one timestamp-less line was dropped) and Loki had no stream for that pod inside the authorized window ending 2026-11-24T09:34:57Z, so the exact message at each exit is unknown.
When and by whom MEMORY="16Mi" was written into ConfigMap platform-policy-controller-server is unknown; change_history is not integrated in this run and the ConfigMap view carried no managedFields.
Which of the five MutatingWebhookConfigurations actually delivers the pod patch cannot be determined, since all of them resolve to the same service platform-ops/platform-policy-controller.
Impact on callers beyond the frontend was not measured: no other service showed its own error spans in the 09:34:38-09:34:46 sample, and requests after 09:34:57 are outside the authorized window.
The deleted pods nginx-thrift-68bc7d94df-477lv and nginx-thrift-65f656c999-gvltj no longer exist, so only their partial log lines are available.
next_steps: Confirm from cluster audit logs or the policy controller that pod CREATE in social-network is being mutated to 16Mi, and review why a policy controller is enforcing memory limits on this namespace.
After correcting the injection, recreate the nginx-thrift pod and confirm limits.memory returns to 256Mi, restart count stops increasing, and Endpoints for service nginx-thrift show a ready address.

Add monitoring for containers whose memory limit is orders of magnitude below observed working set, and for Services whose Endpoints have zero ready addresses, so a single crash-looping frontend pod is detected directly.
Re-check the wrk2 load generator rounds after recovery to confirm throughput returns to the ~102 req/s seen in round #0 without write socket errors.

import base64
import json
import ssl
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

MEMORY = "16Mi"

def build_patch(resources):
    """Emit JSON Patch ops that stamp MEMORY into both
    resources.requests.memory and resources.limits.memory on container[0].
    RFC 6902 "add" semantics: replaces the value if the target already exists,
    so this works whether the field is absent or already populated."""
    ops = []
    if resources is None:
        ops.append({
            "op": "add",
            "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources",
            "value": {"requests": {"memory": MEMORY}, "limits": {"memory": MEMORY}},
        })
        return ops
    if resources.get("requests") is None:
        ops.append({"op": "add", "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources/requests",
                    "value": {"memory": MEMORY}})
    else:
        ops.append({"op": "add", "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources/requests/memory",
                    "value": MEMORY})
    if resources.get("limits") is None:
        ops.append({"op": "add", "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources/limits",
                    "value": {"memory": MEMORY}})
    else:
        ops.append({"op": "add", "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources/limits/memory",
                    "value": MEMORY})
    return ops

class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        length = int(self.headers.get("content-length", "0") or 0)
        raw = self.rfile.read(length)
        uid = ""
        patch = []
        try:
            body = json.loads(raw)
            uid = body.get("request", {}).get("uid", "")
            containers = body.get("request", {}).get("object", {}).get("spec", {}).get("containers", [])
            if containers:
                patch = build_patch(containers[0].get("resources"))
        except Exception:
            pass

        resp = {"uid": uid, "allowed": True}
        if patch:
            resp["patchType"] = "JSONPatch"
            resp["patch"] = base64.b64encode(json.dumps(patch).encode()).decode()
        response = {
            "apiVersion": "admission.k8s.io/v1",
            "kind": "AdmissionReview",
            "response": resp,
        }
        data = json.dumps(response).encode()
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(data)

    def log_message(self, fmt, *args):
        return

httpd = HTTPServer(("0.0.0.0", 8443), Handler)
